title: constraint_model.ipynb

canonical_node.axiom: A strategy is admissible only if it satisfies all six constraints: justice, mercy, freewill, love, entropy, and holiness.
definitions: Constraint function: a function taking a 10-parameter strategy vector and returning True/False based on threshold conditions.

Parameter vector: 10 continuous/discrete parameters including payment_magnitude, cost_to_sinner, coercion_level, relational_access, negentropy_input, corruption_addressed, voluntary_by_redeemer, scope, permanence, source_is_external.
All-passed boolean: True if all six constraint functions return True for a given parameter vector.
derivation: Define six constraint functions with threshold conditions on the parameter vector.
Evaluate a strategy by applying all six constraints and checking if all pass.
Use grid and random search to explore the parameter space for configurations that satisfy all constraints.
Verify uniqueness of the cross configuration by exhaustive search.
canonical_node.action: Given a strategy parameter vector, evaluate all six constraints and return the count of satisfied constraints and whether all are satisfied. Use optimization to search for all-passing configurations.
boundary: Does not define the specific threshold values for each constraint.
Does not apply the model to specific biblical strategies; that is the role of test09_constraint_satisfaction.ipynb.
Does not extend to 100,000 random trials; that is the role of free_body_model.ipynb.
test: For any parameter vector, the constraint functions return deterministic True/False.
The optimization search should find no all-passing configuration other than the cross configuration.
The notebook should be reproducible in Google Colab.

dg1_dependencies: Python runtime with numpy and matplotlib (typical Colab environment).
dg_protocol.dg2_new_capability: Provides a reusable constraint satisfaction engine for evaluating strategies against six constraints.
dg_protocol.dg3_preserved_floor: Preserves the ability to evaluate any strategy parameter vector against the six constraints.
dg_protocol.dg4_collapse_if_removed: Without this model, the formal test (test09) and the Monte Carlo extension (free_body_model) would lack the constraint functions and evaluation framework.

overstatement_risks: The document claims exhaustive search verifies uniqueness, but the search is over a discretized grid and random sampling, not a formal proof.
The threshold values are not specified, so the constraints are not fully defined.
The claim that the cross configuration is the only solution is not formally proven.
kill_conditions: If the constraint functions are not implemented as described.
If the optimization finds an all-passing configuration other than the cross configuration.
If the notebook is not reproducible.
risk.lean_target: Formalize the constraint functions and threshold values, and prove uniqueness of the cross configuration.

plain_summary: This notebook defines a constraint satisfaction engine with six constraints and a 10-parameter strategy space. It evaluates strategies and searches for all-passing configurations, claiming the cross configuration is unique. It is a methodology tool, not a formal proof.
